lines.text: Why is the night sky dark? Think hard.
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ ɪz ðə nˈaɪt skˈaɪ dˈɑːɹk? θˈɪŋk hˈɑːɹd.

lines.text: Say the universe has no edge or start. Then every line of sight would end on a star. Like a forest: every look hits a trunk.
lines.phonemes: sˈeɪ ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs hɐz nˈoʊ ˈɛdʒ ɔːɹ stˈɑːɹt. ðˈɛn ˈɛvɹi lˈaɪn ʌv sˈaɪt wʊd ˈɛnd ˌɔn ɐ stˈɑːɹ. lˈaɪk ɐ fˈɔːɹɪst: ˈɛvɹi lˈʊk hˈɪts ɐ tɹˈʌŋk.

lines.text: Far stars look fainter, but there are more of them. Those two effects cancel, so the whole sky should glow like a star's surface.
lines.phonemes: fˈɑːɹ stˈɑːɹz lˈʊk fˈeɪntɚ, bˌʌt ðɛɹˌɑːɹ mˈɔːɹ ʌv ðˌɛm. ðoʊz tˈuː ɪfˈɛkts kˈænsəl, sˌoʊ ðə hˈoʊl skˈaɪ ʃˌʊd ɡlˈoʊ lˈaɪk ɐ stˈɑːɹz sˈɜːfɪs.

lines.text: The key here is time. Far starlight may not have had time to reach us yet. We now put the universe's age near thirteen point eight billion years.
lines.phonemes: ðə kˈiː hˈɪɹ ɪz tˈaɪm. fˈɑːɹ stˈɑːɹlaɪt mˈeɪ nˌɑːɾɐv hæd tˈaɪm tə ɹˈiːtʃ ˌʌs jˈɛt. wiː nˈaʊ pˌʊt ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːsᵻz ˈeɪdʒ nˌɪɹ θˈɜːtiːn pˈɔɪnt ˈeɪt bˈɪliən jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: Past a certain distance, starlight is still on its way. So we can only see so far. The dark sky hints that the universe has a beginning.
lines.phonemes: pˈæst ɐ sˈɜːʔn dˈɪstəns, stˈɑːɹlaɪt ɪz stˈɪl ˌɔn ɪts wˈeɪ. sˌoʊ wiː kæn ˈoʊnli sˈiː sˈoʊ fˌɑːɹ. ðə dˈɑːɹk skˈaɪ hˈɪnts ðætðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs hɐz ɐ bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ.

lines.text: So tonight's dark isn't empty. It's a clue: the universe has not been shining forever.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ tənˈaɪts dˈɑːɹk ˌɪzənt ˈɛmpti. ɪts ɐ klˈuː: ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs həznɑːt bˌɪn ʃˈaɪnɪŋ fɚɹˈɛvɚ.

lines.text: Light time: from the Sun, about eight minutes. From the farthest galaxies we see, billions of years.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt tˈaɪm: fɹʌmðə sˈʌn, ɐbˌaʊt ˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts. fɹʌmðə fˈɑːɹðɪst ɡˈælɐksiz wiː sˈiː, bˈɪliənz ʌv jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: Next: where did the gold in your ring come from?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌɛɹ dˈɪd ðə ɡˈoʊld ɪn jʊɹ ɹˈɪŋ kˈʌm fɹʌm?
